newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC INTO ITALIAN OPEN SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC INTO ITALIAN OPEN SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Croatian Goran Ivanisevic, the highest-ranked survivor at the Italian Open, reached the semifinals on Friday with a composed victory over Australia's Scott Draper, conqueror of defending champion Thomas Muster earlier in the week.
A break in each set was sufficient for the number six seed, playing his first tournament since breaking a finger last March, to win the quarterfinal 6-4 6-4 in just over an hour.
In an even match played in hot and humid conditions, it was the Croat's ability to take his chances that settled the match.
Describing himself as "rested" after a five-week break from the game, the often erratic Ivanisevic for once kept his cool on the pressure points.
He broke the unseeded Australian on his only two break points of the match -- at 3-2 in the first set and 4-3 in the second.
By contrast, the inexperienced Draper, competing in his first clay court quarter-final, failed to take the two break points he was offered.
"I'm surprised. Usually I don't play well on clay. This is different. After five weeks, I'm hungry," said Ivanisevic.
The break is his longest stint without tennis since a knee operation in 1994 kept him off the tour for eight weeks.
"I didn't touch a racket for 20 days. I had fun. I watched other sports. I didn't think about tennis. Now I'm fresh for this event and the French," he added.
Ivanisevic is just one of three seeds left in a tournament that lost its top five ranked players in the opening four days.
The other survivors are number seven seed Marcelo Rios of Chile and Spanish 10th seed Alex Corretja.

The world's top two players, Pete Sampras and Michael Chang, were eliminated in the first round, Austria's Muster and Dutch Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek went in the second and world number five Yevgeny Kafelnikov fell on Thursday.
Saturday will now see Ivanisevic's fourth semi at the Italian Open although he has only reached the final once, in 1993, when he lost to American Jim Courier.
Courier, unseeded here but twice a champion, will meet Rios in the quarters with Spain's Alberto Berasategui playing German Marc-Kevin Goellner.
Ivanisevic will play either Corretja or Moroccan Karim Alami, who defeated the Croat in Barcelona last month. Alami, from Casablanca, is the first Moroccan player to reach the last eight in Rome.
